claim_judgments.rationale: Claim C0000 faithfully captures the baseline composition of a flight review under 14 CFR 61.56(a), including the minimum ground and flight training hours and the cross-referenced exceptions in paragraphs (b) and (f).
Claim C0001 accurately preserves the mandatory content elements of the flight review specified in 14 CFR 61.56(a)(1) and (a)(2), covering both units U0001 and U0002.

Claim C0002 correctly states the glider pilot substitution option under 14 CFR 61.56(b), preserving the permission modality, the minimum three flights requirement, and traffic pattern altitude qualification.

Claim C0003 fully preserves the prohibition against acting as pilot in command without a flight review and logbook endorsement within the 24-calendar-month window under 14 CFR 61.56(c), retaining all exceptions and conditions covering units U0004 and U0005.

Claim C0004 faithfully states the exemption from the flight review requirement under 14 CFR 61.56(d)(1) for individuals passing a pilot proficiency check or practical test within the 24-calendar-month period.
Claim C0005 consolidates and faithfully represents the flight instructor practical test exemptions under 14 CFR 61.56(d)(2)(i)-(iv), satisfying units U0007, U0008, U0009, and U0010.
Claim C0006 accurately describes the exemption under 14 CFR 61.56(e) for completing one or more phases of an FAA-sponsored pilot proficiency program within the 24-calendar-month period.

Claim C0007 accurately conveys the flight instructor ground training exemption under 14 CFR 61.56(f), including both alternative qualifying tracks under paragraphs (f)(1) and (f)(2), covering units U0012 and U0013.
Claim C0008 accurately states the student pilot exemption under 14 CFR 61.56(g), including all conditions regarding certificate training and a current solo flight endorsement under § 61.87.

Claim C0009 correctly captures the permission under 14 CFR 61.56(h) allowing flight review requirements to be accomplished in combination with § 61.57 and recent experience requirements at instructor discretion.
Claim C0010 accurately conveys the condition in 14 CFR 61.56(i)(1) requiring simulation device usage to follow an approved course conducted by a part 142 training center.
Claim C0011 properly states the condition and exception in 14 CFR 61.56(i)(2) concerning takeoff and landing requirements under § 61.57 when using a flight simulator not approved for landings.
Claim C0012 accurately preserves the condition in 14 CFR 61.56(i)(3) that the simulator or device must represent an aircraft or set of aircraft for which the pilot is rated.

Claim C0001 explicitly includes the requirement to review the general operating and flight rules of part 91.

Claim C0002 faithfully retains the glider pilot substitution rule with all associated criteria.

Claim C0003 retains the requirement to have a logbook endorsement from the authorized instructor certifying satisfactory completion of the review.
Claim C0004 covers the flight review exemption for passing a pilot proficiency check or practical test within the 24-month period.

Claim C0005 covers the exemption for passing an examiner practical test for an additional rating on a flight instructor certificate.
Claim C0005 covers the exemption for passing an examiner practical test to meet flight instructor recent experience requirements under § 61.197(b)(1).
Claim C0005 covers the exemption for passing an examiner practical test for reinstatement of flight instructor privileges under § 61.199(b)(2).
Claim C0006 covers the exemption for completing one or more phases of an FAA-sponsored pilot proficiency program.
Claim C0007 covers the ground training exemption based on completing recent experience requirements for a flight instructor certificate under § 61.197.
Claim C0007 covers the ground training exemption based on completing an approved flight instructor refresher course under § 61.199(a)(1).
Claim C0008 covers the flight review exemption for student pilots undergoing training with a valid solo endorsement.
Claim C0009 captures the option to combine flight review requirements with § 61.57 and recent experience requirements.
